summary: Aboard the doomed Titanic, upper-class Rose falls in love with penniless Jack; the ship sinks into freezing water and he dies saving her.

hunger.why: First-class dinners and the steerage party are social scenes, not matters of appetite.

thirst.why: No one seeks or lacks water.

feeling-cold-hot.why: The sinking plunges everyone into freezing water; Jack dies of the cold while Rose waits on the door.

curiosity.why: Rose discovers the steerage world and the ship's bow with Jack, a light touch of exploration.

explanation-seeking.why: Brock Lovett's salvage team searches for the Heart of the Ocean and listens to old Rose to learn what happened.

skill-acquisition.why: Jack teaches Rose to spit and shows her his drawings, small lessons.

play.why: Dancing and drinking at the steerage party is a burst of play.

resource-accumulation.why: The Heart of the Ocean diamond, Cal's fortune, and the salvage hunt put wealth in view.

resource-foraging.why: Lovett's expedition searches the wreck for the diamond, and the ending reveals where it is.

mental-time-travel.why: Old Rose recalls the voyage, framing the story as memory.

fear-of-predators.why: No animal or monster threatens anyone.

fear-of-aggressors.why: Cal has Jack framed and later hunts the couple with a pistol through the flooding ship.

fear-of-heights.why: Rose climbs over the stern rail, and as the ship upends passengers fall from the vertical deck.

pain-aversion.why: Passengers die of hypothermia and injury in the sinking, including Jack.

pride.why: Jack shouts that he is king of the world, and the builders boast of the unsinkable ship.

shame.why: Rose's mother dreads social disgrace if Rose does not marry Cal.

moral-pride.why: Rose chooses freedom over wealth, Jack gives his life for her, and the band plays on as the ship sinks.

guilt.why: Ismay slinks into a lifeboat in shame, and Rose carries survivor's guilt in old age.

warmth.why: Jack's generosity and Molly Brown's kindness contrast with first-class coldness.

moral-blame.why: Cal's cruelty and the locked gates on steerage are condemned, and Ismay is blamed for the speed.

moral-praise.why: Old Rose honors Jack as the man who saved her in every way.

revenge.why: Cal plants the diamond on Jack to punish him.

compassion.why: Jack talks Rose off the rail, Rose frees Jack from the flooding cell, and strangers help each other in the sinking.

affiliation.why: Rose seeks out Jack's company and his steerage friends against her class.

friendship.why: Jack's friends Fabrizio and Tommy are a light touch.

sadness.why: Jack's death in the water and old Rose's memories of him are the film's grief.

humor.why: Jack's spitting lesson and Molly Brown's quips lighten the romance.

embarrassment.why: Jack in a borrowed tuxedo among the first class is lightly awkward.

reasoning.why: Jack holds his own in the dinner-table sparring with Cal.

coalitional-affiliation.why: First class and steerage are separate worlds, and the gates between them matter in the sinking.

status-seeking.why: Cal's arrogance and Rose's mother's drive to secure position through marriage shape the conflict.

envy.why: Cal cannot bear that Rose prefers a penniless artist, a note of envy.

anger.why: Cal's rage when Rose defies him and his pursuit with the gun.

hatred.why: Cal loathes Jack and relishes his arrest.

romantic-affiliation.why: The love story of Jack and Rose, from the bow of the ship to the final promise, is the whole film.

sexual-attraction.why: The drawing scene and the lovemaking in the car play on desire.

long-term-love.why: Rose keeps her promise to Jack and loves him for the rest of her life.

romantic-jealousy.why: Cal's fury at losing Rose to Jack drives his villainy.

sexual-jealousy.why: Cal finds the nude drawing left for him and reacts as a sexual rival.

sexual-disgust.why: Cal's possessive abuse of Rose is treated as coercive.

parental-care.why: Mothers comfort children as the ship sinks, and Rose's mother controls her daughter's future.

familial-love.why: Rose's strained bond with her mother and old Rose with her granddaughter are minor.
